title: Regional Finance Controller - Kenya
description:
Location: Nairobi, Kenya (for exceptional candidates, we are open to other countries where IRW has a country office in the African region) Contract: Permanent Salary: £38,322 Closing Date: 11th October 2026 Islamic Relief Worldwide (IRW) is a faith-based humanitarian and development organisation working to save and transform the lives of some of the world's most vulnerable people. Established in 1984 and operating in over 45 countries, we respond to emergencies, tackle poverty, empower communities, and advocate for lasting change. We are seeking an experienced and strategic Regional Finance Controller - Africa (West and East) to join our Finance & Corporate Services Division. This is a unique opportunity for a senior finance leader who is passionate about financial governance, capacity building, compliance, and driving sustainable improvement across complex international operations. The preferred location for this role is Nairobi, Kenya. However, we recognise that exceptional talent exists across the continent and will consider applications from suitably qualified candidates located within Africa who can support the regional travel requirements and responsibilities of the position. The Finance & Corporate Services Division is a strategic enabler of organisational performance, accountability and sustainability, delivering integrated services across Finance, Treasury, ERP & Digital Transformation, ICT, Supply Chain and Facilities. As part of an ambitious finance transformation programme, the division is strengthening financial governance, independent oversight, service excellence, and data-driven decision making across the organisation's global footprint. About the Role The Regional Finance Controller (RFC) is responsible for providing financial oversight, governance, assurance, compliance, and capacity building across Islamic Relief's country offices and implementing partners throughout West and East Africa. This is far more than a traditional financial control role. You will work closely with Country Directors, Finance Managers, operational teams, and local partners to strengthen financial management practices, build organisational capability, and ensure the highest standards of financial stewardship are embedded across the region. You will play a critical leadership role in improving financial performance, enhancing internal control frameworks, strengthening donor and statutory compliance, and supporting long-term financial sustainability. Through visible, hands-on engagement with country offices and partners, you will help drive a step-change in financial discipline, transparency, accountability, and decision-making. The role combines strategic oversight with practical delivery. You will be responsible for assessing financial performance, mentoring regional finance teams, identifying and mitigating risk, supporting fraud prevention initiatives, and ensuring finance effectively supports programme delivery and donor confidence. Reporting to the Global Finance Operations Lead, you will provide expert technical guidance and leadership across a diverse and complex regional portfolio, supporting the ongoing evolution of Islamic Relief's global finance operating model. The successful candidate will spend approximately 50% of their time travelling across the region, providing direct support to country offices, finance teams, and implementing partners. The Successful Candidate Will Have: A professionally recognised accounting qualification (ACCA, CIMA, ICAEW, ICMA or equivalent). Significant senior-level financial management experience, ideally within the humanitarian, NGO, development, or international non-profit sector. Demonstrable experience leading financial governance, compliance, assurance, and internal control activities across multiple entities or geographical locations. Strong expertise in budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, financial planning, and scenario analysis. Experience producing consolidated management accounts, variance analysis, financial performance reporting, and strategic financial insight. Proven experience managing donor compliance requirements and statutory obligations. A strong understanding of financial risk management, fraud prevention, and control frameworks. Experience leading, developing, mentoring, and coaching finance teams. Excellent stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and support both finance and non-finance leaders. Strong communication skills and the ability to present complex financial information clearly and effectively. Experience designing and delivering finance training, capability building, and development programmes. High levels of integrity, accountability, professionalism, and cultural sensitivity. Commitment to the mission, vision, and values of Islamic Relief Worldwide. Fluency in both English and French. Desirable Experience managing donor-funded programmes and institutional grant reporting within international NGOs. Experience working in fragile, conflict-affected, or complex operating environments. Strong understanding of the geopolitical, regulatory, and socio-economic contexts across Africa. Experience supporting finance transformation, organisational change, or continuous improvement initiatives. Experience working with local implementing partners and sub-grantees. Why Join Islamic Relief? This role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact across multiple countries by strengthening financial performance, governance, accountability, and sustainability throughout one of the world's leading humanitarian organisations. If you are a strategic finance leader who enjoys developing people, improving systems, driving compliance, and enabling operational excellence across international programmes, we would love to hear from you. For more information, please refer to the full Job Description and Person Specification. If you are talented, reliable, service-minded, resilient, and highly motivated, with a strong commitment to Islamic Relief's mission and values of Sincerity, Excellence, Compassion, Social Justice, and Custodianship, please submit your application via our online recruitment portal. PLEASE NOTE: Interviews may be held on an ongoing basis, and we reserve the right to close this vacancy prior to the advertised closing date should a suitable candidate be identified. Pre-Employment Checks Any employment with Islamic Relief will be subject to: Proof of eligibility to live and work within the UK. Satisfactory references. Appropriate screening and safeguarding checks. Please note that we are only able to consider applications from candidates who already have the right to work in the UK. Sponsorship is not available for this position. Our Values and Commitment to Safeguarding Islamic Relief is committed to preventing all forms of abuse, exploitation, harassment, discrimination, and financial misconduct. We expect all employees and volunteers to share this commitment and uphold the highest standards of conduct. All appointments are subject to satisfactory references and safeguarding checks, including participation in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme where applicable. Islamic Relief is an equal opportunities employer.

How to Apply: **For further details about the role and application requirements, please refer to the full Job Description and Person Specification and apply via our online recruitment portal using the link below.** [**Regional Finance Controller**](https://islamic-relief.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4327242?cid=1858&t=Regional-Finance-Controller)

title: Country Director, Ethiopia
description:
Job Title: Country Director, Ethiopia Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia (Only candidates who are eligible to work legally without work visa sponsorship in Ethiopia will be considered.) Contract Type: Full-time (40 hours per week), 1-year fixed term contract with possibility of renewal based on funding and performance. This is a national position. Hiring Salary: ETB 508,934 per month (before taxes) Target Start Date: January 2027 Application Closing Date: October 20, 2026 23:59 EAT This job advert is for an existing vacancy. About Right To Play: For more than 25 years, Right To Play has been protecting, educating, and empowering millions of children each year to rise above adversity through the power of play. We offer programs in 10 countries across Africa, Asia, the Middle East and North America, reaching millions of children each year in some of the most difficult places on earth, helping them to connect, learn and thrive. We do this by harnessing play, one of the most fundamental forces in a child's life, to equip children with the critical skills they need to dismantle barriers and embrace opportunities, in learning and in life. This work is supported by our two global offices in Toronto, Canada and London, UK; and seven National Offices in North America and Europe. Right To Play in Ethiopia is working with government, civil society organizations, communities, teachers and parents to increase access to quality education, enhance primary school children's learning and social emotional skills, promote children's access to inclusive, high quality, play-based Early Childhood Care and Education, provide play-based psychosocial support to improve the holistic well-being of children and young people and address the challenges that children face in host, internally displaced and refugee communities. Learn more about our programs in Ethiopia from our website . Benefits Highlights: Connect and collaborate with a global team who are passionate about protecting, educating and empowering children and youth using the power of play! Culture premised on our Culture Code (accept everyone, make things happen, display courage, demonstrate care, and be playful) Paid leave (20 days annual leave and 3 personal days per year) Competitive benefits such as medical insurance for employee and eligible family members, life insurance for employee, transportation allowance, and communications allowance 10% temporary allowance for Ethiopia employees from October to December 2026 and the next salary review is in January 2027 Learning opportunities and 5 learning and development (L&D) days per year Flexible work arrangements More information on what we offer is available on our website . Job Description: Job Title: Country Director (CD) Grade: 11 Reports to: Vice President, Transformation and Impact Location: Ethiopia Direct Reports: Program Manager, Education Specialist, Finance Manager, People and Culture Specialist, MEL Specialist, Logistics Officer Department: Global Program Unit 1.Purpose: Provides overall strategic and programmatic leadership including business development, fundraising, compliance and risk, financial and people management to ensure the success and growth of the country programme. 2.Accountability & Responsibilities: Governance and representation (20%) Identifies and manages organisational risk , including legal and governance matters, and acts as RTP’s legal representative in country. Represents RTP at country level , engaging government, donors, UN agencies, and NGO coordination platforms to build influence, credibility, and strategic partnerships. Fundraising and Communication (20%) Leads country-level fundraising and resource mobilisation , driving proposal development, donor engagement, and diversified funding partnerships. Leads in-country media and external engagement , strengthening RTP’s profile and ensuring alignment with organisational values and objectives. Strategy development and implementation (15%) Sets and leads the strategic direction of the country programme , ensuring alignment with RTP strategy, national priorities, and legal and regulatory requirements. Programmatic oversight, learning and innovation (15%) Oversees the country programme portfolio , ensuring high-quality delivery, measurable impact for children and young people, and timely reporting to donors, government, and HQ. Promotes collaboration and learning , advising partners on play-based and sport-for-development approaches and embedding evidence-informed practice. Champions innovation and continuous improvement , driving excellence in programming and efficiency across internal systems and processes. Operational management (15%) Provides strategic oversight of finance and administration , including budgeting, expenditure control, audits, grant compliance, and strong internal controls. Holds overall accountability for safeguarding, safety, and security , ensuring compliance with RTP policies and national legislation. Staff and workplace management (15%) Ensures effective people management , including recruitment, performance management, learning and development, payroll, and the promotion of a safe and inclusive culture. Leads, mentors, and develops a diverse country team , fostering staff wellbeing, inclusion, and high performance. Promote Safeguarding, foster a safe, respectful, and accountable work environment by modelling appropriate conduct and addressing any behaviour that undermines a healthy workplace. Perform other duties as assigned 3.Scope (geographical and/or functional), Impact and Autonomy: Oversees all aspects of the country office, providing guidance and support to the team, while serving on the Global Leadership Team to ensure quality program delivery, adherence to budgets, and contributing to global initiatives that enhance organizational systems and processes. 4.Leadership and Staff Management: Leads and develops the Country Management Team through coaching, mentoring, and capability-building while championing a safe, inclusive, and high-performing culture. Oversees People & Culture processes to ensure compliance, best practices, and effective performance management, upholding strong DEIA standards, staff safety, and well-being. Demonstrates integrity and resilience, proactively addressing and mitigating legal risks, including seeking legal advice when necessary. 5.Information Requirement for Decision-Making: Makes decisions based on a combination of internal and external information, often requiring an analytic approach to draw conclusions from incomplete information or non-conclusive information. 6.Innovation and Improvements Drives innovation and continuous improvement to deliver high-quality, impactful programs and more efficient internal systems and ways of working. 7. Relationships & Communications: Internal / External: Builds and sustains strategic relationships with key stakeholders, including donors, government officials, UN agencies, academia, media, NGOs, and local partners, while promoting RTP’s identity and relevance to the needs of vulnerable populations, in alignment with the localization strategy. Leads strategic donor, HQ visits, workshops, represents RTP in high-level meetings, conferences, and media to strengthen its profile. 8. Expertise (Certifications / Education, Professional Experience): Extensive experience in leadership roles within a large or medium international development organization, including: strategic planning, leadership and people management, project management and planning, monitoring and evaluation and financial and risk management. Master’s degree in business administration, social sciences, development studies or related discipline. Experience working in or managing programmes in stable and fragile contexts. Proven success with mobilizing new sources of program funding. Understanding of laws, regulations and cultural dynamics local and international. Fluency in spoken and written Amharic and English Significant experience with a child-focused organization is desirable. 9.Core Competences: Collaboration: Highly collaborative with strong interpersonal skills; excels at working in with a multicultural team and builds rapport and trust to develop strong external partnerships. Growth Mindset: Demonstrates commitment to own professional development and encourages their team to develop their potential, creates a learning culture through effective coaching and mentorship. Communication: Communicates complex operational, technical & strategic issues clearly & credibly to diverse audiences, leveraging strong networks to secure donor funding & influence stakeholders. Resilience: Strong organizational skills and the ability to work under pressure: multi-tasking, meeting deadlines, solving problems creatively and embracing challenges with resilience. Professionalism: Models professionalism and RTP’s values, promoting a safe, inclusive workplace and positive impact for children and youth. Management and Interpersonal Skills : Lead and mentor country team with influence, fostering trust, high performance, and shared ownership of outcome. 10.Additional Information: Expected to travel regularly domestically and occasionally internationally and work outside regular hours.

title: RESPONSABLE DU BUREAU DE PLAIDOYER ET DE LIAISON AUPRÈS DE L’UNION AFRICAINE, Oxfam en Afrique
description:
Type de contrat : Contrat à durée déterminée de 2 ans Grade interne : B1, International Rémunération : conforme à la grille salariale d’Oxfam International. Cette offre comprend les avantages sociaux de base ainsi que les prestations globales applicables au personnel recruté à l’international et relocalisé.Nous considérons que les modalités de travail flexibles sont essentielles pour bâtir le Secrétariat de demain. Nous sommes donc disposés à échanger avec vous sur les modalités susceptibles de vous convenir. Le poste Oxfam en Afrique recherche une personne expérimentée, dotée d’un leadership reconnu et d’un forte capacité d’influence, pour diriger son Bureau de plaidoyer et de liaison auprès de l’Union africaine (UA), basé à Addis-Abeba. En tant que membre de l’Équipe de direction de la Plateforme Afrique, vous piloterez l’engagement d’Oxfam auprès de l’Union africaine et de ses institutions. Vous élaborerez et mettrez en œuvre des stratégies de plaidoyer à fort impact afin d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques à l’échelle continentale. Vous représenterez Oxfam au plus haut niveau auprès de l’UA, nouerez des relations stratégiques et contribuerez à positionner Oxfam comme un partenaire crédible et de confiance. Ce poste joue un rôle central dans la réalisation de la mission d’Oxfam en Afrique : il établit un lien entre les espaces d’élaboration des politiques continentales et les réalités nationales, tout en veillant à ce que les actions de plaidoyer soient cohérentes, porteuses d’impact et ancrées dans les réalités vécues par les communautés. Ce poste relève de la Direction Afrique, avec un rattachement matriciel à la Direction Plaidoyer, Campagnes et Engagement (ACE). Profil recherché Nous recherchons une personne reconnue pour son leadership en matière de plaidoyer et d’influence, disposant d’une solide expérience de collaboration avec l’Union africaine ou des institutions multilatérales comparables. Vous avez démontré votre capacité à concevoir et à mettre en œuvre des stratégies d’influence porteuses d’impact, combinant analyse des politiques, plaidoyer, communication médiatique et partenariats afin de favoriser des changements significatifs. Vous excellez dans l’établissement de relations et la négociation, savez évoluer efficacement dans des environnements complexes associant de multiples parties prenantes et êtes en mesure d’exercer une influence au plus haut niveau. Grâce à votre capacité de réflexion stratégique et d’analyse politique, vous savez traduire les processus de l’UA en possibilités concrètes d’influence et d’impact pour les pays et les partenaires. Votre expérience du leadership vous permet de diriger des équipes diversifiées et de travailler au sein d’un réseau mondial, tout en favorisant la collaboration et la redevabilité. Vous avez une connaissance approfondie du contexte sociopolitique africain et adhérez aux approches féministes, décoloniales et portées par les partenaires. La maîtrise professionnelle de l’anglais et du français est indispensable. Pourquoi nous rejoindre Ce poste offre une occasion rare d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques au plus haut niveau continental. À Oxfam, vous façonnerez notre engagement auprès de l’Union africaine, piloterez le plaidoyer sur des enjeux majeurs tels que les inégalités, la pauvreté et la justice, et collaborerez avec des gouvernements, des diplomates et des institutions internationales pour réaliser des changements concrets. Au sein d’une équipe de direction diversifiée et collaborative, vous contribuerez à rapprocher les politiques continentales des réalités des communautés, afin que les décisions prises au plus haut niveau se traduisent par des résultats tangibles pour les populations partout en Afrique. Ce que nous offrons À Oxfam, nous sommes convaincus que chaque aspect de notre travail peut contribuer à un changement positif. Si vous partagez cette conviction et possédez les compétences nécessaires pour relever les défis liés à ce poste, cette fonction vous offrira de grandes possibilités d’épanouissement personnel ainsi que d’excellentes perspectives d’évolution professionnelle. Oxfam s’engage à proposer une rémunération équitable, sur la base d’une semaine de travail de 36 heures À propos de nous Oxfam est un mouvement mondial de personnes qui agissent ensemble pour mettre fin à l’injustice qu’est la pauvreté. Cela signifie que nous nous attaquons aux inégalités qui maintiennent les populations dans la pauvreté. Ensemble, nous sauvons des vies, protégeons les populations et les aidons à reconstruire leur existence. Lorsqu’une catastrophe survient, nous aidons les personnes à bâtir un avenir meilleur, pour elles-mêmes et pour les autres. Nous agissons sur des enjeux tels que les droits fonciers, le changement climatique et les discriminations à l’égard des femmes. Et nous ne nous arrêterons pas tant que chaque personne sur la planète ne pourra pas vivre à l’abri de la pauvreté. Nous sommes une confédération internationale composée de 22 organisations affiliées et du Secrétariat d’Oxfam International. Avec nos partenaires et les communautés locales, nous menons des actions humanitaires, des programmes de développement et des campagnes dans plus de 76 pays. Oxfam en Afrique (OiA) est une plateforme continentale qui assure la coordination des bureaux pays d’Oxfam en Afrique et collabore avec des organisations de la société civile, des universitaires, des gouvernements et le secteur privé afin de contribuer à une Afrique plus égalitaire, en remettant en cause les structures de pouvoir qui perpétuent les inégalités et les injustices. À cette fin, Oxfam en Afrique apporte un leadership intellectuel dynamique et offre un espace de collaboration à ses partenaires. Oxfam en Afrique joue un rôle moteur dans l’appui aux communautés locales et le renforcement de leur pouvoir d’agir, la promotion de l’égalité de genre, le plaidoyer en faveur de changements de politiques publiques et le renforcement des capacités des organisations locales de la société civile. L’ensemble de notre travail est guidé par nos valeurs fondamentales : Autonomisation, Redevabilité, Inclusion, Courage, Solidarité et Égalité. Notre engagement en matière de safeguarding (Protection contre le harcèlement, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels) Oxfam s’engage à prévenir toute forme de comportement inapproprié au travail, notamment le harcèlement sexuel, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels, les manquements à l’intégrité et les irrégularités financières, ainsi qu’à promouvoir le bien-être des enfants, des jeunes et des adultes. Oxfam attend de l’ensemble de son personnel et de ses volontaires qu’ils partagent cet engagement et respectent notre Code de conduite. Nous accordons une importance primordiale au recrutement de personnes qui partagent nos valeurs et les mettent en pratique. Remarque : Toute offre d’emploi sera subordonnée à la réception de références satisfaisantes et pourra faire l’objet de contrôles appropriés, notamment une vérification du casier judiciaire et des contrôles relatifs au financement du terrorisme. Le Secrétariat d’Oxfam International participe également au Mécanisme interorganisations de divulgation des inconduites (Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme). Conformément à ce dispositif, si une personne candidate a précédemment travaillé pour une autre organisation membre, nous solliciterons auprès de cette organisation des informations concernant toute constatation d’exploitation sexuelle, d’abus sexuels et/ou de harcèlement sexuel survenue pendant son emploi, ainsi que tout incident qui faisait encore l’objet d’une enquête au moment de son départ. En soumettant sa candidature, la personne candidate confirme avoir pris connaissance de cette procédure de recrutement.

How to Apply: **Comment postuler** Si vous souhaitez influencer les politiques continentales et renforcer l’engagement auprès de l’Union africaine afin de favoriser des changements durables en Afrique, nous vous invitons à postuler. Veuillez soumettre un CV à jour et une lettre de motivation via ce lien [https://oxfam.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4325897?cid=3360](https://oxfam.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4325897?cid=3360) , en démontrant clairement en quoi votre profil répond aux critères essentiels définis dans la fiche de poste de Responsable du Bureau de plaidoyer et de liaison auprès de l’Union africaine. Veuillez noter que seules les personnes présélectionnées seront contactées, généralement dans les deux semaines suivant la date de clôture

title: Administrator
description:
EMERGENCY is an independent and neutral international organisation founded in 1994 to provide free, high-quality medical and surgical care to victims of war, landmines and poverty. EMERGENCY promotes a culture of peace, solidarity and respect for human rights. We work in a sustainable way: building healthcare facilities, training local personnel, and conducting search and rescue missions in the Mediterranean Sea. ROSTER POSITION FOR : Sierra Leone, Sudan, OPT, Ukraine, Afghanistan TYPE OF CONTRACT: fixed term contract (6 months), which includes a monthly salary, travel expenses, board and lodgings, insurance cover (liability, health and accident insurance), a period of paid leave to be taken at the end of the mission. The Administrator is responsible for the management of all the administrative and accountancy procedures of the project. BACKGROUND AND ORGANISATION OF WORK The Administrator co-ordinates, supervises and works alongside the non-medical staff, managing the organisation of work and providing them with on-the-job training. The Administrator is responsible to the Country Director and he/she is in regular communication with the Field Operations Department (HQ) regarding all aspects of the job. DUTIES AND REPONSIBILITIES Her/his main duties and responsibilities will be: to ensure all the administrative and accountancy documentation of the project is kept correctly, including that required by the auditors and possible donor organisations; to ensure the correct management of cash, bank accounts, and the reconciliation of accounts on a monthly basis; to ensure the correct administrative management of the national staff (salaries, contracts, holidays, permissions…); to prepare the monthly report (cash flow, statements and reports file…) and present it punctually to HQ, highlighting any possible gaps in the approved budget; to collaborate with the Country Director and HQ in drafting the annual budget for the project; to assist the Country Director in drafting project proposals for institutional donors; to assist the Country Director during audits carried out by donor agencies. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS Diploma in Accountancy or bachelor degree in Economics, Political science or International relations; at least 2 years’ relevant work experience in the administration field; familiarity with the financial guidelines and procedures of the main donor agencies (EU, MAECI, UN agencies…) would be an advantage; experience in managing petty cash; experience in managing revenue and payments; experience in reconciling bank accounts and cash records. REQUIRED AVAILABILITY 6 months’ overseas stay including a period of leave to be taken at the end of the mission in agreement with the Coordinator.

title: Network Development Associate-Africa
description:
Location: Ethiopia, Kenya (as long as HelpAge International holds the registration in this country), Tanzania and Zimbabwe Department : Global Impact- Network Development Reports to (Line Manager): Network Platform Manager Responsible for(Line managing): N/A Grade: Grade A or an equivalent based on the country of hire Contract Type: Open-ended contract About HelpAge HelpAge International works with a diverse global network of around 200 organisations across 99 countries to promote the rights of older people to lead dignified, healthy and secure lives. Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience. As countries prepare for and adapt to population ageing, we are seeking to make a difference at a critical juncture to how societies, economies and institutions adapt to this change. About the Job The Network Development Associate based in Africa will play a key role in strengthening engagement, communication, and coordination across the HelpAge Global Network. This is an exciting opportunity to support a growing and strategically important area of work that helps connect members, amplify their voices, and enable collaboration across regions. The postholder will work closely with the Network Platform Manager, Africa Regional Adviser and Thematic Advisers to support member engagement, knowledge sharing, and the effective functioning of the HelpAge Digital Portal. The role will help build stronger relationships across the network, improve information flows, and contribute to more connected, visible and collaborative ways of working, particularly across Africa and within the wider global network. Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities Network Engagement and support to the Network Platform (50%) Working with the Network Platform Team, strengthen communication and coordination between HelpAge and network members, particularly across Africa, alongside the Regional Advisers and Thematic Advisers. Support and facilitate knowledge sharing, collaboration and peer learning across the network. Support the curation, management and updating of the HelpAge digital portal, providing administrative backend support and firstline user support. Help organise thematic sessions, webinars, peer learning events, and cross‑network exchanges. Support in the development of newsletters and additional communications content for network members and other stakeholders. Support member applications, onboarding, and induction processes. Maintain accurate member information and mailing lists on HelpAge CONNECT (Hosted by salesforce) and SharePoint. Support the coordination of Network Development Team meetings and provide other administrative support to the Network Development Team as needed. Support in tracking engagement and participation trends across the membership. Regional Network Engagement, Communications and Administrative Support for the Regional Adviser, Africa (50%) Support communication and engagement with potential and existing network members across Africa, helping maintain strong information flows between members, the Regional Adviser and cross organisational teams and the wider network. Provide logistical and administrative support for regional meetings, webinars, learning events and member engagements. Prepare and disseminate agendas, invitations, briefing materials and meeting notes, and maintain agreed records and documentation. Support communications, member liaison and event administration for regional initiatives, including the Africa Ageing Conference, Africa Coordination Mechanism and resource mobilisation where required. Collect and maintain member engagement data, feedback and participation information to support reporting, learning and continuous improvement. Coordinate translation and interpretation arrangements for regional communications and events where needed. Gather stories, case studies and learning content from network members and partners across Africa. Develop communications and visibility materials that strengthen member engagement and showcase network impact across the region, including ensuring up-to-date information in digital and website platforms. Maintain regional communications channels including social media pages and support knowledge sharing within Africa and across the wider HelpAge network. Contribute to the strategic planning and reporting processes for Africa region including leading on communication and knowledge management plan for Africa. Skills and experience required At least 3–5 years of experience supporting regional and global network coordination processes, member engagement, event coordination, and administrative functions, ideally within international development, civil society, humanitarian settings, or multi-stakeholder environments. Experience in supporting logistical planning and coordination of sub-regional, regional and global meetings, workshops, webinars, learning events and strategic convenings. Good IT skills and familiarity with digital collaboration, communication and data visualization tools. Strong written communication skills with the ability to produce clear, concise documents, including meeting minutes and action points. Experience supporting online events, webinars, virtual meetings and knowledge‑sharing processes. Basic design and editing skills; familiarity with Canva, WordPress and Mailchimp is desirable. Experience producing and supporting newsletters, digital communications and managing social media channels. Ability to draft and edit news updates, communication content and articles in English. Ability to troubleshoot basic digital platforms, connectivity or login issues during online meetings and events. Fluency in English (written and spoken); additional African UNION or UN language are desirable Ability to manage competing priorities, work under pressure and meet deadlines. Strong organizational and time‑management skills. Good interpersonal skills and experience working in cross‑cultural settings. High level of discretion when handling sensitive information. title: Country Representative for Ethiopia, Based in Addis Ababa
description:
WHAT IS IMPACT INITIATIVES ? OUR AIM: IMPACT aims to shape practices and influence policies in humanitarian and development settings, in order to positively impact the lives of people and their communities. Created in 2010, IMPACT is a Geneva-based NGO and the largest independent data provider in contexts of crisis. We aim to support a range of stakeholders in making better, more informed decisions in humanitarian, stabilisation, and development settings. We believe that a key pathway to better planning and decision-making is direct engagement with local communities. HOW DO WE WORK ? IMPACT takes an initiative-based approach to structuring our programming. Each initiative has a specific aim, operational model, and portfolio of solutions. REACH strengthens evidence-based humanitarian decision-making through efficient data collection, management, and analysis - before, during, and after an emergency. PANDA improves the impact of humanitarian and development interventions through programme design, assessments, and monitoring & evaluation. AGORA promotes localised and multi-sectoral aid action in support of the recovery and stabilisation of crisis-affected communities, in partnership with local stakeholders Through our global team of research specialists, on average IMPACT publishes more than 1,700 information products on a yearly basis. In 2010, IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarters are based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, which particularly allows IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support in its fields of intervention. We are currently looking for a Country Representative to lead our Ethiopia mission, based in Addis Abeba Position: Country Representative Contract duration: 12 months Location: Addis Abeba, Ethiopia, with potential travel to Kampala, Uganda Starting Date: October / November 2026 Application Deadline: 09 October 2026. COUNTRY PROFILE Since 2018, Ethiopia has experienced escalating insecurity and unrest, including large-scale displacement, loss of life, and widespread destruction of property, following significant domestic political changes. These crises have compounded the effects of recurring climate-related shocks affecting large parts of the country. In November 2020, conflict erupted in the northern Tigray region, triggering significant displacement across Tigray, Amhara, and Afar regions. Since August 2023, renewed conflict in Amhara has further intensified humanitarian needs, leading to the declaration of a state of emergency and restrictions on movement across the region. Together, these crises have severely disrupted livelihoods, constrained access to essential goods and staple commodities, and increased the vulnerability of affected populations, placing additional pressure on humanitarian response capacities across the country. FUNCTIONS Under the management of IMPACT’s Regional Coordinator (RC) for Africa in Geneva, the Country Representative (CR) is responsible for representing IMPACT and managing and developing IMPACT’s programmes in Ethiopia. S/he leads the IMPACT team to achieve program excellence and ensure the highest level of impact and accountability, while ensuring compliance to IMPACT guidelines, policies and standards across the mission. The CR is in regular contact with HQ, ensuring that organizational risks are promptly and clearly communicated to the Regional Coordinator and other relevant HQ Senior Management. S/he will promote organizational vision and core values across the mission and will actively link with HQ to contribute to the implementation of IMPACT’s global strategy. In his/her mission, the Country Representative will be hosted by Acted and will fall under the direct responsibility and management of Acted’s Country Director for all Administrative, Security, Logistics and Finance issues. S/he will therefore fully abide by Acted’s Security, HR, Administration and Logistics rules and regulations, and, in coordination with Acted, will ensure that all IMPACT staff abide by them. RESPONSIBILITIES The Country Representative responsibilities include the following: Strategic Leadership Develop and execute an up-to-date Country Strategy aligned with IMPACT’s global objectives and Ethiopia’s humanitarian landscape. Identify strategic opportunities, consolidate ongoing initiatives, and explore new programme areas to enhance IMPACT’s value to the aid community. Programme and Project Management In coordination with the Deputy Country Representative, oversee programme planning, implementation, and evaluation, ensuring all projects meet objectives, timelines, and compliance standards. Facilitate coordination between IMPACT and partner organizations to achieve efficient project delivery and impact. Fundraising and Donor Engagement Identify and secure funding opportunities in collaboration with HQ and Acted. Lead proposal development and negotiate contracts with donors, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities. Operations Support the Operations Managers and Project Development and Partnership Officers in building and maintaining a broad network of partner organizations to strengthen operational capacity and facilitate the implementation of activities in hard-to-reach and underserved areas. Continue to explore alternative operational models and innovative research approaches to expand geographic and population coverage, particularly among marginalized and difficult-to-reach communities. Ensure regular coordination with Acted's project development and FLATS departments (finance, logistics, administration, transparency, security) at all stages of project development and implementation. Finance and Budget Oversight Manage project budgets and forecast expenses, ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting to HQ and Acted. Mitigate financial risks and ensure optimal budget utilization. Human Resources and Team Leadership In consultation with the Deputy Country Representative, guide and develop the IMPACT team, ensuring performance standards, capacity building, and adherence to IMPACT and Acted’s policies. Coordinate with HQ and Acted for transparent recruitment and career management of staff. External Representation and Coordination Establish and maintain productive relationships with donors, UN agencies, NGOs, and other stakeholders, representing IMPACT’s programmes and strategic interests. Ensure proactive contribution to key humanitarian decision-making forums and promote IMPACT’s programme visibility. Data Protection and Accountability Uphold strict confidentiality of all data collected and engage with communities respectfully, ensuring awareness of programme objectives and methods. REQUIREMENTS Academic qualifications: Excellent academic qualifications, including a Master’s degree in a relevant discipline (International Relations, Political Sciences, Social Research, Development Studies, or similar). Management experience: Previous experience in a senior management role in an INGO at field level. Track record in successful management of international and national teams in humanitarian contexts. Familiarity with aid system: Familiarity with the aid system, and the research community. Communication/reporting skills: Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting, including proven experience in contributing to high level presentations/briefings. Years of work experience: At least 5 years of relevant working experience. Any previous experience in Ethiopia would be an asset. Research skills: Experience in assessments. M&E, field research, evaluations an asset. Multi-tasking skills: Ability to multitask with tight deadlines in complex environment. Level of independence: A self-starter with a proven ability to work independently. Cross-cultural work environment: Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment. Language skills: Fluency in English required**.** Security environment: Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment. COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS For this position, salary between 4’050€ and 4’100€ monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 500 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. title: Ethiopia Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer (Fixed-Term)
description:
About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable. The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our permanent team numbers over 180 with nearly 1,000 rural seasonal staff supporting them. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices. About the Role The Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer supports the Ethiopia Trees Program's expansion through desk research, primary data gathering, field verification scoutings, and evidence generation to identify and assess potential expansion opportunities across Ethiopia. The role synthesizes geographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and stakeholder information to support strategic expansion decisions and operational readiness. The officer will participate in field scouting visits with the expansion team to validate desk research findings and gather additional insights. Responsibilities Data Collection & Research Conduct desk research to identify and assess potential program expansion areas across regions, zones, and woredas. Collect, analyze, and synthesize agricultural, environmental, demographic, socioeconomic, market, and government data to support expansion planning. Review secondary data from government institutions, research organizations, development partners, and other credible sources to generate evidence-based insights. Monitor demographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and policy trends to identify opportunities and potential risks for program expansion. Develop and maintain databases, trackers, and research documentation to support expansion planning and operational readiness. Verify, clean, and analyze research and field data to ensure quality, accuracy, consistency, and usability. Support the development and continuous improvement of expansion assessment tools, scoring frameworks, research methodologies, and analytical processes. Field & Stakeholder Verification of Data Participate in field scouting and assessment visits to validate desk research findings and collect additional information. Engage with government offices, development partners, local stakeholders, and other relevant actors to verify data, assumptions, and findings. Assess key expansion criteria, including agroforestry suitability, water availability, land suitability, market potential, operational feasibility, scalability, accessibility, and implementation risks. Identify data gaps and discrepancies and coordinate with relevant stakeholders to obtain and validate additional information. Integrate field observations and stakeholder feedback with secondary data to strengthen expansion assessments and recommendations. Reporting & Collaboration Prepare clear and evidence-based assessment reports, analytical summaries, and recommendations to support expansion decisions. Present research findings and recommendations to relevant teams and stakeholders and contribute to expansion planning discussions. Collaborate with the expansion team and relevant technical and operational teams to translate research findings into actionable expansion plans. Maintain clear documentation of research findings, field validation results, assumptions, and recommendations to support decision-making and future reference Reporting, Stakeholder Engagement & Collaboration Support engagement with government institutions, community representatives, development partners, and other relevant stakeholders during expansion assessments and field scouting activities. Coordinate information gathering, stakeholder consultations, and validation activities to support expansion planning and decision-making. Identify collaboration opportunities that strengthen expansion planning, field implementation, and operational readiness. Prepare high-quality assessment reports, presentations, briefing materials, and regular progress updates for internal and external stakeholders. Document research findings, field observations, lessons learned, stakeholder feedback, and key decisions to support knowledge sharing and continuous improvement. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate research findings and stakeholder insights into actionable recommendations and expansion plans. Track assigned activities and maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation related to expansion research, assessments, and planning. Perform other research and operational support tasks as assigned to advance the Tree Program’s expansion objectives. Support the recruitment of field staff Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people.
